questions.text: What are the two main purposes of PostgreSQL roles?

answers.text: To represent users connecting to the DBMS and to group roles when configuring access
Only to store passwords and network settings

questions.explanation: The notes treat a role both as a user that can connect to the DBMS and as part of a role hierarchy useful for access management.

questions.text: Which role-attribute to purpose mappings are correct? Select all correct answers.
questions.explanation: The slide lists LOGIN, SUPERUSER, CREATEDB, and CREATEROLE; CREATEROLE is related to role management, not tablespaces.

questions.text: Which role attribute is required for a role to be used for an ordinary PostgreSQL connection?
questions.explanation: LOGIN directly indicates that a role can log in to a PostgreSQL session.

questions.text: Which statements about creating roles are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A role can be created with CREATE ROLE
Role attributes can be specified when it is created
Login capability is determined by the LOGIN attribute
Every new role automatically receives SUPERUSER

questions.explanation: CREATE ROLE creates a role and lets you define its properties. SUPERUSER is not granted automatically.

questions.text: In which file does PostgreSQL define client-access rules and authentication methods?
questions.explanation: The notes define pg_hba.conf as the host-based authentication file containing connection rules.

questions.text: Which fields are considered when choosing a matching pg_hba.conf record in the structure shown? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Name of the SQL table accessed by the first query

questions.explanation: A pg_hba.conf row is matched against connection parameters including type, database, user, and for network connections the address.

questions.text: How does PostgreSQL choose a rule from pg_hba.conf?

answers.text: It scans rows from top to bottom and uses the first matching one
It collects all matching rows and combines them
It always uses the last matching row

questions.explanation: Record order is fundamental: the first row matching the connection parameters is selected.

source.locator: Scanning pg_hba.conf from top to bottom

questions.text: What happens after the first matching pg_hba.conf row is found? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The authentication method specified by the row is applied
The role's ability to log in is checked
The CONNECT privilege on the database is checked
If authentication fails, the next matching row is automatically tried

questions.explanation: The material emphasizes that after the first row is selected, the relevant checks are performed and later rows are not considered.

questions.text: What does the local connection type mean in pg_hba.conf?

answers.text: A connection only to the postgres database

questions.explanation: In the pg_hba.conf diagram, local corresponds to a local socket and host to TCP/IP.

questions.text: Which mappings between PostgreSQL authentication methods and their purposes are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: trust — allow the connection without checking a password
peer — obtain user information from the operating system
scram-sha-256 — always allow the connection without authentication

questions.explanation: The slide directly maps trust to allowing access, reject to denial, peer to OS-based checking, and scram-sha-256 and md5 to password authentication.

questions.text: Which authentication method for local connections obtains the user name from the operating system?
questions.explanation: The material describes peer as the method that obtains the user name from the operating system.

questions.text: Which methods are password-authentication methods? Select all correct answers.
questions.explanation: The slide groups scram-sha-256 and md5 as methods in which the client is asked for a password.

questions.text: What happens if no pg_hba.conf row matches a new connection?

answers.text: The server creates a matching rule

questions.explanation: pg_hba.conf rules form an explicit access list. If no record matches, the connection is not allowed.

questions.text: Which conditions must be satisfied for a successful connection in the model shown? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A matching pg_hba.conf record must be found
Authentication specified by that record must succeed
The role must have LOGIN and the required CONNECT access
The role must always be SUPERUSER

questions.explanation: A connection is determined by several checks: the pg_hba.conf rule, the authentication method, and the role's privileges.

questions.text: The peer method is enabled for roles alice and bob. Why is changing pg_hba.conf alone not enough for a successful login?

answers.text: The operating-system user must be mapped correctly to the PostgreSQL role

questions.explanation: The exercise first asks you to verify that peer login is impossible without the required OS-user mapping.

questions.text: Which actions are needed to configure and verify authentication rules for the alice and bob roles? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Create the alice and bob roles
Test allowed and rejected connections under different settings
Grant both roles SUPERUSER to test peer

questions.explanation: The practical part is built around creating roles, modifying pg_hba.conf, and testing the behavior of different authentication rules.

questions.text: How can a PostgreSQL client provide a password? Select all correct answers.
questions.explanation: The password-authentication section lists manual entry, the PGPASSWORD variable, and the ~/.pgpass file. pg_hba.conf selects the authentication method but does not store the role password.

source.locator: Slide 7: supplying a password on the client

questions.text: What permissions should the ~/.pgpass file have on Unix?

answers.text: 0600 — only the owner can read and modify the file
0644 — the file must be readable by everyone
0777 — execute permission is required for everyone
PostgreSQL clients do not check the file permissions

questions.explanation: The material states that ~/.pgpass must be accessible only to its owner; PostgreSQL ignores the file if its permissions are broader.

questions.text: Which statements about applying connection settings are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: After pg_hba.conf is changed, the server must reload the configuration
pg_reload_conf() can be used to reload pg_hba.conf
listen_addresses determines the network interfaces on which PostgreSQL accepts TCP connections
Changing pg_hba.conf automatically creates new roles with LOGIN

questions.explanation: pg_hba.conf takes effect after reload. listen_addresses controls network listening, while pg_hba.conf controls access and the authentication method for incoming connections.

questions.text: In which system catalog does PostgreSQL store role password information that ordinary users cannot access?
questions.explanation: The password-authentication material identifies pg_authid as the system catalog that stores the role password verifier/hash.

questions.text: What is pg_ident.conf used for together with the peer method?

answers.text: To map an operating-system user name to a PostgreSQL role
To store the role password hash
To select the WAL segment size

questions.explanation: In the DBA1 exercise, pg_ident.conf defines a map that lets peer authentication map the OS user student to the PostgreSQL roles alice and bob.

source.locator: Slide 23: pg_ident.conf and the stmap map
